pattern: Feature-first modular monolith, split into two npm workspaces (server, client) under one repo. Every server module owns a disjoint URL subtree and never imports another module's internals — cross-stage data flows as request/response payloads (duck-typed local contracts) or through server/src/shared/, never direct module-to-module imports.

modules.name: auth
modules.note: Reserved: registration/login/JWT sessions/role guards. Downstream generated apps get full auth via the Security Engine (Phase 7) — this scaffold is the platform's own (still-pending) user auth, not a gap in what NexArch generates.

modules.name: database-designer
modules.note: One module folder exports two AppModules (databaseModule + openapiModule)

modules.name: review
modules.note: Reserved for a future post-generation static-analysis/optimization pass distinct from Phase 12's Quality Engine.

layeringConvention.frontendFeatureShape: <feature>-page.tsx + components/ + use-<feature>.ts hooks, backed by shared/services/*.service.ts (axios) and shared/types/api.ts (the one client-side mirror of every server contract)
layeringConvention.enforcementEvidence: Verified live: the Architecture Validator (Phase 12's own architecture-validator.ts) scored 100/100 'Controller/service layer separation' across all 8 generated backend modules in the end-to-end smoke test, using the identical check this report applies conceptually to NexArch's own module tree.

moduleIsolationAudit.rule: "Modules are islands" — a module may import ../../shared/* or its own relative paths, never a sibling module's internals.
moduleIsolationAudit.method: grep across server/src/modules for import paths reaching into another module directory
moduleIsolationAudit.falsePositivesExcluded: Import-statement-shaped strings inside the code generators (backend-generator, frontend-generator, security-engine) are template content for the DOWNSTREAM generated app's own files, not real imports in NexArch's module graph.

server: shared/middleware (security, rate-limiter, request-context, request-logger, error-handler, validate)
client: shared/components/ui (button, card, badge, dialog, dropdown-menu, toaster, ...)
shared/services (one *.service.ts per module's client API surface)

namingConventions.server: kebab-case files, camelCase functions/variables, PascalCase types/interfaces — verified via ESLint (zero errors) plus a manual sample of every module directory name
namingConventions.client: kebab-case files except PascalCase React components, same camelCase/PascalCase split as server — verified via ESLint (zero errors)
namingConventions.apiRoutes: REST-ish, versioned under /api/v1, resource-first paths (/projects, /project/:id) except where a phase's own spec dictated a specific literal path set (Phase 10/12 mount at basePath '/' for exactly this reason)

serverFilesOverThreshold.assessment: acceptable — a domain lookup table (data), not dense control flow
acceptable — template-literal code emitter; most lines are the generated app's source text

clientFilesOverThreshold.assessment: known tradeoff — single append-only type-mirror file, one per platform-wide convention since Phase 1; splitting by domain (types/deployment.ts, types/quality.ts, ...) would be a genuine architecture change outside this pass's "verify and polish, don't redesign" mandate. Recommended for a future phase, not fixed now.
acceptable — a rich single-page dashboard, not excessive for its scope
